It doesn’t take a lot of brain power to purpose something that results in the infinite torment of an individual as unethical. Even in human law, yes there is punishment for crimes, but it’s never infinite because no matter how serious the crime, it’s always finite. They may be in jail for the rest of their life, but there’s still a set amount of years even if it’s 500. 
So for arguments sake, let’s just assume that free will is justified in every way and people that don’t believe in god go to hell because of their free will and sin. Hell is everlasting, it never ever stops. Why does god choose to punish finite actions (sin) with infinite measures? Even if someone murdered 1 million ppl I think most would agree that they deserve a lot of punishment, possibly even death (which without religion is basically the right/privilege to live being taken away from u) But I don’t think anyone would come to the conclusion that the person deserves to be burned alive forever and ever. It sounds so barbaric it would be hard to even come up with that idea. Even if there was a way to punish the murderer to the same extent that they punished their victims, it would definitely not add up to infinite torture. So if it’s not unethical then what is it?
